verses.kjv: But the children of Belial said, How shall this man save us? And they despised him, and brought him no presents. But he held his peace.
verses.decoded: But the worthless people said, How can this man save us? They looked down on him and did not give him any gifts. But he remained silent.

verses.kjv: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabesh-gilead: and all the men of Jabesh said unto Nahash, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve thee.
verses.decoded: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up and camped against Jabesh-gilead, and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, 'Make a treaty with us, and we will serve you.'

verses.kjv: And Nahash the Ammonite answered them, On this condition will I make a covenant with you, that I may thrust out all your right eyes, and lay it for a reproach upon all Israel.
verses.decoded: And Nahash the Ammonite answered them, I will make a treaty with you only if I can gouge out all your right eyes, and make it a disgrace for all Israel.

verses.kjv: And the elders of Jabesh said unto him, Give us seven days’ respite, that we may send messengers unto all the coasts of Israel: and then, if there be no man to save us, we will come out to thee.
verses.decoded: And the elders of Jabesh said to him, Give us seven days' delay, so that we can send messengers to all parts of Israel; and then, if no one comes to save us, we will come out to you.

verses.kjv: Then came the messengers to Gibeah of Saul, and told the tidings in the ears of the people: and all the people lifted up their voices, and wept.
verses.decoded: Then the messengers went to Gibeah of Saul and told the news to the people. All the people shouted loudly and cried.

verses.kjv: And, behold, Saul came after the herd out of the field; and Saul said, What aileth the people that they weep? And they told him the tidings of the men of Jabesh.
verses.decoded: And Saul came after the herd out of the field; and Saul said, What is wrong with the people that they are crying? And they told him the news about the men of Jabesh.

verses.kjv: And the Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard those tidings, and his anger was kindled greatly.
verses.decoded: The Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard that news, and he became very angry.

verses.kjv: And he took a yoke of oxen, and hewed them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the coasts of Israel by the hands of messengers, saying, Whosoever cometh not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done unto his oxen. And the fear of the Lord fell on the people, and they came out with one consent.
verses.decoded: He took a pair of oxen, cut them into pieces, and sent the pieces throughout all the regions of Israel by messengers, saying, Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, the same will be done to his oxen. The fear of the LORD came upon the people, and they came out united.

verses.kjv: And when he numbered them in Bezek, the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
verses.decoded: When he counted them at Bezek, the Israelites were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah were thirty thousand.

verses.kjv: And they said unto the messengers that came, Thus shall ye say unto the men of Jabesh-gilead, To morrow, by that time the sun be hot, ye shall have help. And the messengers came and shewed it to the men of Jabesh; and they were glad.
verses.decoded: And they said to the messengers who came, "This is what you should say to the men of Jabesh-gilead: Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you will have help." And the messengers went and told the men of Jabesh, and they were glad.

verses.kjv: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, To morrow we will come out unto you, and ye shall do with us all that seemeth good unto you.
verses.decoded: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us whatever seems good to you.

verses.kjv: And it was so on the morrow, that Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the host in the morning watch, and slew the Ammonites until the heat of the day: and it came to pass, that they which remained were scattered, so that two of them were not left together.
verses.decoded: The next day, Saul divided the people into three groups; they entered the middle of the enemy camp during the early morning watch and killed the Ammonites until the heat of the day. The survivors were scattered so widely that not even two of them stayed together.

verses.kjv: And the people said unto Samuel, Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death.
verses.decoded: And the people said to Samuel, Who is the person that said, 'Shall Saul rule over us?' Bring the men so we can put them to death.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day the Lord hath wrought salvation in Israel.
verses.decoded: And Saul said, No one will be put to death today, because today the LORD has brought salvation to Israel.

verses.kjv: Then said Samuel to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.
verses.decoded: Then Samuel said to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.

verses.kjv: And all the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before the Lord in Gilgal; and there they sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings before the Lord; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.
verses.decoded: All the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king in the presence of the LORD at Gilgal. They offered peace offerings to the LORD there, and Saul and all the men of Israel were very happy.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto all Israel, Behold, I have hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me, and have made a king over you.
verses.decoded: And Samuel said to all Israel, Look, I have listened to your request in everything you told me, and I have appointed a king over you.

verses.kjv: And now, behold, the king walketh before you: and I am old and grayheaded; and, behold, my sons are with you: and I have walked before you from my childhood unto this day.
verses.decoded: And now, look, the king is walking in front of you; I am old and have gray hair; and look, my sons are here with you; and I have led you from my childhood until today.

verses.kjv: Behold, here I am: witness against me before the Lord, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.
verses.decoded: Look, here I am. Testify against me before the LORD and before his chosen one: whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated? Whom have I oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe to ignore it? I will return it to you.

verses.kjv: And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man’s hand.
verses.decoded: And they said, You have not cheated us, nor oppressed us, nor taken anything from anyone.

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, The Lord is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that ye have not found ought in my hand. And they answered, He is witness.
verses.decoded: And he said to them, The LORD is a witness against you, and his anointed one is a witness today, that you have not found anything in my hand. And they answered, He is a witness.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto the people, It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And Samuel said to the people, It is the LORD who appointed Moses and Aaron, and who brought your ancestors out of the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: Now therefore stand still, that I may reason with you before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord, which he did to you and to your fathers.
verses.decoded: Now, stand still so I can explain to you in the presence of the LORD all the good things the LORD has done for you and your ancestors.

verses.kjv: When Jacob was come into Egypt, and your fathers cried unto the Lord, then the Lord sent Moses and Aaron, which brought forth your fathers out of Egypt, and made them dwell in this place.
verses.decoded: When Jacob came to Egypt, and your ancestors cried out to the LORD, then the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your ancestors out of Egypt and made them live in this place.

verses.kjv: And when they forgat the Lord their God, he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.
verses.decoded: When they forgot the LORD their God, he allowed Sisera, the commander of the army of Hazor, the Philistines, and the king of Moab to defeat them, and they fought against them.

verses.kjv: And they cried unto the Lord, and said, We have sinned, because we have forsaken the Lord, and have served Baalim and Ashtaroth: but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve thee.
verses.decoded: And they cried out to the LORD and said, We have sinned because we have abandoned the LORD and served Baalim and Ashtaroth. But now, please save us from the power of our enemies, and we will serve you.

verses.kjv: And the Lord sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side, and ye dwelled safe.
verses.decoded: And the LORD sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and rescued you from the power of your enemies all around, and you lived safely.

verses.kjv: And when ye saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, ye said unto me, Nay; but a king shall reign over us: when the Lord your God was your king.
verses.decoded: And when you saw that Nahash, the king of the Ammonites, was coming against you, you said to me, No; but we want a king to rule over us, even though the LORD your God was your king.

verses.kjv: Now therefore behold the king whom ye have chosen, and whom ye have desired! and, behold, the Lord hath set a king over you.
verses.decoded: So now, look at the king you have chosen and wanted! The LORD has appointed a king over you.

verses.kjv: If ye will fear the Lord, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the Lord your God:
verses.decoded: If you fear the LORD, serve him, obey his voice, and do not rebel against the LORD's command, then both you and the king who rules over you will continue to follow the LORD your God.

verses.kjv: But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers.
verses.decoded: But if you do not obey the voice of the LORD and rebel against the command of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against you, just as it was against your ancestors.

verses.kjv: Now therefore stand and see this great thing, which the Lord will do before your eyes.
verses.decoded: So now stand and watch this amazing thing that the LORD will do right in front of you.

verses.kjv: Is it not wheat harvest to day? I will call unto the Lord, and he shall send thunder and rain; that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the Lord, in asking you a king.
verses.decoded: Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, and he will send thunder and rain; so that you may understand and see that your sin is great, which you have done in the presence of the LORD, by asking for a king.

verses.kjv: So Samuel called unto the Lord; and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.
verses.decoded: So Samuel prayed to the LORD; and the LORD sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people were very afraid of the LORD and Samuel.

verses.kjv: And all the people said unto Samuel, Pray for thy servants unto the Lord thy God, that we die not: for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king.
verses.decoded: And all the people said to Samuel, Pray for your servants to the LORD your God, so that we do not die; because we have added this evil to all our sins, asking for a king.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto the people, Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness: yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart;
verses.decoded: And Samuel said to the people, Do not be afraid: you have done all this evil: but do not turn away from following the LORD, instead serve the LORD with all your heart;

verses.kjv: And turn ye not aside: for then should ye go after vain things, which cannot profit nor deliver; for they are vain.
verses.decoded: Do not turn away, because then you would follow worthless things that cannot help or save you; they are useless.

verses.kjv: For the Lord will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake: because it hath pleased the Lord to make you his people.
verses.decoded: For the LORD will not abandon his people because of his great name: because the LORD has been pleased to make you his people.

verses.kjv: Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way:
verses.decoded: As for me, I pray to God that I will never sin against the LORD by stopping my prayers for you. Instead, I will teach you what is good and right.

verses.kjv: Only fear the Lord, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you.
verses.decoded: Only respect the LORD, and serve him sincerely with all your heart, because think about how great things he has done for you.

verses.kjv: But if ye shall still do wickedly, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king.
verses.decoded: But if you continue to do evil, you and your king will be destroyed.

verses.kjv: Saul reigned one year; and when he had reigned two years over Israel,
verses.decoded: Saul was king for one year; and when he had been king over Israel for two years,

verses.kjv: Saul chose him three thousand men of Israel; whereof two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in mount Beth-el, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin: and the rest of the people he sent every man to his tent.
verses.decoded: Saul selected three thousand men from Israel; two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and on Mount Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent each back to his own home.

verses.kjv: And Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, Let the Hebrews hear.
verses.decoded: And Jonathan attacked the Philistine soldiers stationed in Geba, and the Philistines found out about it. Then Saul blew the trumpet all over the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear."

verses.kjv: And all Israel heard say that Saul had smitten a garrison of the Philistines, and that Israel also was had in abomination with the Philistines. And the people were called together after Saul to Gilgal.
verses.decoded: All Israel heard that Saul had defeated a group of Philistine soldiers, and that Israel was also hated by the Philistines. The people gathered together behind Saul at Gilgal.

verses.kjv: And the Philistines gathered themselves together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the sea shore in multitude: and they came up, and pitched in Michmash, eastward from Beth-aven.
verses.decoded: The Philistines gathered together to fight against Israel, with thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and people as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They advanced and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.

verses.kjv: When the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait, (for the people were distressed,) then the people did hide themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in high places, and in pits.
verses.decoded: When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble, because the people were upset, the people hid themselves in caves, bushes, among rocks, on high places, and in pits.

verses.kjv: And some of the Hebrews went over Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. As for Saul, he was yet in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
verses.decoded: Some of the Hebrews crossed the Jordan River into the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people followed him, shaking with fear.

verses.kjv: And he tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.
verses.decoded: He waited seven days, as Samuel had told him to, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people left him.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.
verses.decoded: And Saul said, Bring a burnt offering to me and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, that he might salute him.
verses.decoded: It happened that as soon as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him to greet him.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, What hast thou done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash;
verses.decoded: And Samuel said, What have you done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that you did not come within the appointed days, and that the Philistines had gathered together at Michmash;

verses.kjv: Therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now upon me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication unto the Lord: I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering.
verses.decoded: So I said, The Philistines are going to attack me here at Gilgal, and I have not prayed to the LORD. So I forced myself and offered a burnt offering.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.
verses.decoded: And Samuel said to Saul, You have acted foolishly: you have not obeyed the command of the LORD your God, which he commanded you: for now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.

verses.kjv: But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the Lord hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the Lord commanded thee.
verses.decoded: But now your kingdom will not last: the LORD has looked for a man after his own heart, and the LORD has appointed him to be leader over his people, because you did not obey what the LORD commanded you.

verses.kjv: And Samuel arose, and gat him up from Gilgal unto Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people that were present with him, about six hundred men.
verses.decoded: And Samuel got up and went from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. Saul counted the people who were with him, about six hundred men.

verses.kjv: And Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people that were present with them, abode in Gibeah of Benjamin: but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
verses.decoded: Saul, his son Jonathan, and the people with them stayed in Gibeah of Benjamin, while the Philistines set up camp in Michmash.

verses.kjv: And the spoilers came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned unto the way that leadeth to Ophrah, unto the land of Shual:
verses.decoded: And the raiders came out of the Philistine camp in three groups: one group turned toward the road that leads to Ophrah, to the land of Shual:

verses.kjv: And another company turned the way to Beth-horon: and another company turned to the way of the border that looketh to the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
verses.decoded: Another group turned toward Beth-horon, and another group turned toward the border road that faces the valley of Zeboim, toward the wilderness.

verses.kjv: Now there was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel: for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make them swords or spears:
verses.decoded: At that time, there was no blacksmith to be found anywhere in the land of Israel because the Philistines said, 'We don't want the Hebrews to make swords or spears.'

verses.kjv: But all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, to sharpen every man his share, and his coulter, and his axe, and his mattock.
verses.decoded: But all the Israelites went to the Philistines to sharpen each man's plowshare, his coulter, his axe, and his mattock.

verses.kjv: Yet they had a file for the mattocks, and for the coulters, and for the forks, and for the axes, and to sharpen the goads.
verses.decoded: But they had a file for the mattocks, and for the plow blades, and for the forks, and for the axes, and to sharpen the goads.

verses.kjv: So it came to pass in the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people that were with Saul and Jonathan: but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found.
verses.decoded: On the day of the battle, none of the people with Saul and Jonathan had a sword or spear in their hands; only Saul and his son Jonathan had them.

verses.kjv: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the passage of Michmash.
verses.decoded: The Philistine soldiers went out to the road near Michmash.

verses.kjv: Now it came to pass upon a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said unto the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines’ garrison, that is on the other side. But he told not his father.
verses.decoded: One day, Jonathan, the son of Saul, said to the young man carrying his armor, "Come, let us go over to the Philistines' outpost on the other side." But he did not tell his father.

verses.kjv: And Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which is in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men;
verses.decoded: Saul stayed in the farthest part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree in Migron, and the people with him were about six hundred men.

verses.kjv: And Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, I-chabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the Lord’s priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.
verses.decoded: Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, brother of I-chabod, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, the LORD’s priest in Shiloh, was wearing an ephod. The people did not know that Jonathan had left.

verses.kjv: And between the passages, by which Jonathan sought to go over unto the Philistines’ garrison, there was a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
verses.decoded: And between the paths that Jonathan tried to cross to reach the Philistines' camp, there was a sharp rock on one side and a sharp rock on the other side: the name of one was Bozez, and the name of the other was Seneh.

verses.kjv: The forefront of the one was situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah.
verses.decoded: The front part of one was located to the north, facing Michmash, and the other was to the south, facing Gibeah.

verses.kjv: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the Lord will work for us: for there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few.
verses.decoded: And Jonathan said to the young man carrying his armor, Come, and let us go over to the fortress of these uncircumcised people: maybe the LORD will help us, because the LORD can save whether by many or by few.

verses.kjv: And his armourbearer said unto him, Do all that is in thine heart: turn thee; behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.
verses.decoded: And his armor-bearer said to him, Do everything that is in your heart: turn around; look, I am with you according to your heart.

verses.kjv: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto these men, and we will discover ourselves unto them.
verses.decoded: Then Jonathan said, Look, we will cross over to these men, and we will reveal ourselves to them.

verses.kjv: If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them.
verses.decoded: If they say to us, 'Wait until we come to you,' then we will stay where we are and will not go up to them.

verses.kjv: But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up: for the Lord hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign unto us.
verses.decoded: But if they say, 'Come up to us,' then we will go up, because the LORD has given them into our hands; and this will be a sign for us.

verses.kjv: And both of them discovered themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.
verses.decoded: And both of them revealed themselves to the Philistine soldiers; and the Philistines said, Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they had hidden themselves.

verses.kjv: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armourbearer, Come up after me: for the Lord hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.
verses.decoded: The men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armor-bearer and said, "Come up to us, and we will show you something." Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Come up after me, because the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel."

verses.kjv: And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armourbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him.
verses.decoded: And Jonathan climbed up using his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer following him; the enemies fell in front of Jonathan, and his armor-bearer killed them behind him.

verses.kjv: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armourbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were an half acre of land, which a yoke of oxen might plow.
verses.decoded: And the first killing, which Jonathan and his armor-bearer did, was about twenty men, within about half an acre of land, which a pair of oxen could plow.

verses.kjv: And there was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling.
verses.decoded: There was shaking in the army, in the battlefield, and among all the people: the soldiers in the camp and the raiders also shook, and the ground shook: it was a very great shaking.

verses.kjv: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another.
verses.decoded: The guards of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and they saw the crowd breaking apart and continuing to fight each other.

verses.kjv: Then said Saul unto the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there.
verses.decoded: Then Saul said to the people who were with him, "Count now and see who is missing from us." When they had counted, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto Ahiah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.
verses.decoded: And Saul said to Ahiah, Bring here the ark of God. Because the ark of God was at that time with the people of Israel.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the noise that was in the host of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thine hand.
verses.decoded: While Saul was talking to the priest, the noise among the Philistine army continued and grew louder. Saul said to the priest, "Take your hand away."

verses.kjv: And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man’s sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture.
verses.decoded: Saul and all the people with him gathered together and went to the battle, and every man's sword was against his fellow, causing a very great defeat.

verses.kjv: Moreover the Hebrews that were with the Philistines before that time, which went up with them into the camp from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.decoded: Also, the Hebrews who had been with the Philistines before that time, who went with them into the camp from the surrounding countryside, switched sides and joined the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.

verses.kjv: Likewise all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.
verses.decoded: Similarly, all the men of Israel who had hidden themselves on Mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines were running away, also chased after them vigorously in the battle.

verses.kjv: So the Lord saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over unto Beth-aven.
verses.decoded: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle moved on to Beth-aven.

verses.kjv: And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted any food.
verses.decoded: The men of Israel were very troubled that day because Saul had commanded the people, saying, 'Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, so that I can take revenge on my enemies.' Therefore, none of the people ate any food.

verses.kjv: And all they of the land came to a wood; and there was honey upon the ground.
verses.decoded: And all the people from the land came to a forest; and there was honey on the ground.

verses.kjv: And when the people were come into the wood, behold, the honey dropped; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath.
verses.decoded: When the people entered the forest, honey was dripping, but no one put their hand to their mouth because the people were afraid of breaking the oath.

verses.kjv: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.
verses.decoded: But Jonathan did not hear when his father commanded the people with the oath; so he reached out the end of the rod that was in his hand, dipped it into a honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes became bright.

verses.kjv: Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food this day. And the people were faint.
verses.decoded: Then one of the people answered and said, Your father strictly commanded the people with an oath, saying, 'Cursed is the man who eats any food today.' And the people were weak.

verses.kjv: Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.
verses.decoded: Then Jonathan said, My father has caused trouble in the land: look, please, how my eyes have been opened, because I tasted a little of this honey.

verses.kjv: How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?
verses.decoded: How much more, if perhaps the people had eaten freely today from the plunder of their enemies that they found? For wouldn't there have been a much greater slaughter among the Philistines now?

verses.kjv: And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint.
verses.decoded: They struck the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people were very exhausted.

verses.kjv: And the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground: and the people did eat them with the blood.
verses.decoded: And the people rushed to the plunder, took sheep, oxen, and calves, and killed them on the ground; and the people ate them with the blood.

verses.kjv: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the Lord, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day.
verses.decoded: Then they told Saul, saying, Look, the people have sinned against the LORD because they ate food with the blood still in it. And he said, You have broken the law; bring me a large stone today.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the Lord in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.
verses.decoded: And Saul said, Spread out among the people and tell them, Bring me here each man his ox and each man his sheep, and kill them here and eat; and do not sin against the LORD by eating with the blood. And all the people brought each man his ox with him that night and killed them there.

verses.kjv: And Saul built an altar unto the Lord: the same was the first altar that he built unto the Lord.
verses.decoded: And Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first altar he built to the LORD.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatsoever seemeth good unto thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God.
verses.decoded: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines at night and plunder them until the morning light, and let us not leave any of them alive. And they said, Do whatever seems good to you. Then the priest said, Let us come near here to God.

verses.kjv: And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.
verses.decoded: Saul asked God for guidance, 'Should I go down after the Philistines? Will you deliver them into the hands of Israel?' But God did not answer him that day.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Draw ye near hither, all the chief of the people: and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day.
verses.decoded: And Saul said, Come near here, all the leaders of the people, and understand and see where this sin has been committed today.

verses.kjv: For, as the Lord liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.
verses.decoded: As the LORD lives, who saves Israel, even if it is in Jonathan my son, he must die. But not a single person among all the people answered him.

verses.kjv: Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee.
verses.decoded: Then he said to all Israel, Stand on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will stand on the other side. And the people said to Saul, Do what seems good to you.

verses.kjv: Therefore Saul said unto the Lord God of Israel, Give a perfect lot. And Saul and Jonathan were taken: but the people escaped.
verses.decoded: Therefore Saul said to the LORD God of Israel, 'Give a clear and exact lot.' And Saul and Jonathan were chosen, but the people escaped.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken.
verses.decoded: Saul said, 'Cast lots between me and my son Jonathan.' The lot fell on Jonathan.

verses.kjv: Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die.
verses.decoded: Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what you have done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I only tasted a little honey with the end of the rod that was in my hand, and now I must die.

verses.kjv: And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.
verses.decoded: And Saul answered, 'May God do this and even more: because you will surely die, Jonathan.'

verses.kjv: And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.
verses.decoded: And the people said to Saul, Should Jonathan die, who has brought this great victory to Israel? Absolutely not: as the LORD lives, not a single hair on his head will fall to the ground; because he has worked with God today. So the people saved Jonathan, and he did not die.

verses.kjv: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines: and the Philistines went to their own place.
verses.decoded: Then Saul stopped chasing the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their own land.

verses.kjv: So Saul took the kingdom over Israel, and fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines: and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them.
verses.decoded: So Saul became king over Israel and fought against all his enemies on every side: against Moab, against the people of Ammon, against Edom, against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines. Wherever he went, he troubled them.

verses.kjv: And he gathered an host, and smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them.
verses.decoded: He gathered an army, attacked the Amalekites, and rescued Israel from those who were plundering them.

verses.kjv: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchi-shua: and the names of his two daughters were these; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:
verses.decoded: Saul's sons were Jonathan, Ishui, and Melchi-shua. His two daughters were named Merab, the firstborn, and Michal, the younger.

verses.kjv: And the name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz: and the name of the captain of his host was Abner, the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.
verses.decoded: The name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz, and the name of the commander of his army was Abner, the son of Ner, who was Saul’s uncle.

verses.kjv: And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
verses.decoded: Kish was Saul's father, and Ner, who was Abner's father, was the son of Abiel.

verses.kjv: And there was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul: and when Saul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he took him unto him.
verses.decoded: There was intense war against the Philistines throughout all the days of Saul's reign, and whenever Saul saw a strong or brave man, he brought him to his side.

verses.kjv: Samuel also said unto Saul, The Lord sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people, over Israel: now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the Lord.
verses.decoded: Samuel also said to Saul, The LORD sent me to anoint you to be king over his people, over Israel: now therefore listen to the voice of the words of the LORD.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the Lord of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD of hosts says: I remember what Amalek did to Israel, how he ambushed them on the road when they came up from Egypt.

verses.kjv: Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.
verses.decoded: Now go and attack Amalek, and completely destroy everything they have, and do not spare them; kill both men and women, infants and babies, oxen and sheep, camels and donkeys.

verses.kjv: And Saul gathered the people together, and numbered them in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.
verses.decoded: Saul gathered the people together and counted them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men from Judah.

verses.kjv: And Saul came to a city of Amalek, and laid wait in the valley.
verses.decoded: Saul went to a city of the Amalekites and waited in the valley.

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto the Kenites, Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.
verses.decoded: And Saul said to the Kenites, Go away, leave, and separate yourselves from among the Amalekites, so that I do not destroy you along with them; because you showed kindness to all the children of Israel when they came up from Egypt. So the Kenites left the Amalekites.

verses.kjv: And Saul smote the Amalekites from Havilah until thou comest to Shur, that is over against Egypt.
verses.decoded: And Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah until you reach Shur, which is opposite Egypt.

verses.kjv: And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.
verses.decoded: He captured Agag, the king of the Amalekites, alive, and completely destroyed all the people with the sword.

verses.kjv: But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them: but every thing that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly.
verses.decoded: But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, the oxen, the fattened calves, the lambs, and everything that was good, and they did not completely destroy them; however, they completely destroyed everything that was worthless and rejected.

verses.kjv: Then came the word of the Lord unto Samuel, saying,
verses.decoded: Then the message from the LORD came to Samuel, saying,

verses.kjv: It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king: for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments. And it grieved Samuel; and he cried unto the Lord all night.
verses.decoded: I regret that I made Saul king because he has turned away from following me and has not obeyed my commands. This made Samuel very sad, and he prayed to the LORD all night.

verses.kjv: And when Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning, it was told Samuel, saying, Saul came to Carmel, and, behold, he set him up a place, and is gone about, and passed on, and gone down to Gilgal.
verses.decoded: When Samuel got up early to meet Saul in the morning, someone told Samuel, "Saul has come to Carmel, and he has set up a monument for himself, then he went on his way and has gone down to Gilgal."

verses.kjv: And Samuel came to Saul: and Saul said unto him, Blessed be thou of the Lord: I have performed the commandment of the Lord.
verses.decoded: And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, Blessed are you by the LORD: I have carried out the LORD's command.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?
verses.decoded: And Samuel said, What does this bleating of the sheep in my ears mean, and the lowing of the oxen that I hear?

verses.kjv: And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites: for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed.
verses.decoded: And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites because the people spared the best of the sheep and the oxen to sacrifice to the LORD your God; but we have completely destroyed the rest.

verses.kjv: Then Samuel said unto Saul, Stay, and I will tell thee what the Lord hath said to me this night. And he said unto him, Say on.
verses.decoded: Then Samuel said to Saul, Stop, and I will tell you what the LORD has told me tonight. And Saul said to him, Continue.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel, and the Lord anointed thee king over Israel?
verses.decoded: And Samuel said, When you were insignificant in your own eyes, were you not made the leader of the tribes of Israel, and did the LORD not anoint you king over Israel?

verses.kjv: And the Lord sent thee on a journey, and said, Go and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they be consumed.
verses.decoded: And the LORD sent you on a mission and said, Go and completely destroy the sinful Amalekites, and fight against them until they are completely destroyed.

verses.kjv: Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the Lord?
verses.decoded: So why did you not obey the voice of the LORD, but instead rushed to take the spoil and did what was wrong in the eyes of the LORD?

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto Samuel, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.
verses.decoded: And Saul said to Samuel, Yes, I have obeyed the voice of the LORD, and have gone the way the LORD sent me, and have brought Agag, the king of Amalek, and have completely destroyed the Amalekites.

verses.kjv: But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God in Gilgal.
verses.decoded: But the people took some of the plunder, sheep and cattle, the best of the things that should have been completely destroyed, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
verses.decoded: And Samuel said, Does the LORD take as much pleasure in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in obeying the LORD's voice? Look, obeying is better than sacrifice, and listening is better than the fat of rams.

verses.kjv: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.
verses.decoded: For rebellion is like the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is like sin and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, he has also rejected you from being king.

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.
verses.decoded: And Saul said to Samuel, I have sinned because I disobeyed the command of the LORD and your words, because I was afraid of the people and listened to their voice.

verses.kjv: Now therefore, I pray thee, pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the Lord.
verses.decoded: So now, I ask you, forgive my sin and come back with me so that I can worship the LORD.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto Saul, I will not return with thee: for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.
verses.decoded: And Samuel said to Saul, I will not go back with you, because you have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel.

verses.kjv: And as Samuel turned about to go away, he laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle, and it rent.
verses.decoded: As Samuel turned to leave, he grabbed the edge of his robe, and it tore.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto him, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.
verses.decoded: And Samuel said to him, The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and has given it to one of your neighbors who is better than you.

verses.kjv: And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent.
verses.decoded: And also the Strength of Israel does not lie or change His mind, because He is not a human being who would change His mind.

verses.kjv: Then he said, I have sinned: yet honour me now, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and turn again with me, that I may worship the Lord thy God.
verses.decoded: Then he said, I have sinned; but please honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel, and come back with me so that I may worship the LORD your God.

verses.kjv: So Samuel turned again after Saul; and Saul worshipped the Lord.
verses.decoded: So Samuel turned back after Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.

verses.kjv: Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately. And Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.
verses.decoded: Then Samuel said, Bring Agag, the king of the Amalekites, to me. And Agag came to him carefully. And Agag said, Surely the worst part of death is over.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.
verses.decoded: And Samuel said, Just as your sword has made women unable to have children, so your mother will be unable to have children among women. And Samuel cut Agag into pieces in front of the LORD at Gilgal.

verses.kjv: Then Samuel went to Ramah; and Saul went up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.
verses.decoded: Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house in Gibeah, the city of Saul.

verses.kjv: And Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death: nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul: and the Lord repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.decoded: And Samuel did not come to see Saul again until the day he died; however, Samuel grieved for Saul, and the LORD regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.

verses.kjv: And the Lord said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Beth-lehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons.
verses.decoded: The LORD said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go; I am sending you to Jesse from Bethlehem, because I have chosen a king from among his sons."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, How can I go? if Saul hear it, he will kill me. And the Lord said, Take an heifer with thee, and say, I am come to sacrifice to the Lord.
verses.decoded: And Samuel said, How can I go? If Saul hears it, he will kill me. And the LORD said, Take a young cow with you, and say, I have come to offer a sacrifice to the LORD.

verses.kjv: And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will shew thee what thou shalt do: and thou shalt anoint unto me him whom I name unto thee.
verses.decoded: And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you should do: and you will anoint for me the one whom I name to you.

verses.kjv: And Samuel did that which the Lord spake, and came to Beth-lehem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou peaceably?
verses.decoded: And Samuel did what the LORD said, and went to Bethlehem. The elders of the town were afraid when he arrived and asked, Are you coming in peace?

verses.kjv: And he said, Peaceably: I am come to sacrifice unto the Lord: sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
verses.decoded: And he said, Calm down: I have come to offer a sacrifice to the LORD; make yourselves holy and come with me to the sacrifice. And he made Jesse and his sons holy and invited them to the sacrifice.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely the Lord’s anointed is before him.
verses.decoded: When they arrived, he looked at Eliab and said, Surely the LORD’s chosen one is here before me.

verses.kjv: But the Lord said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.
verses.decoded: But the LORD said to Samuel, Do not look at his face or how tall he is, because I have rejected him; for the LORD does not see as humans see; humans look at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.

verses.kjv: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, Neither hath the Lord chosen this.
verses.decoded: Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him pass in front of Samuel. But Samuel said, The LORD has not chosen this one either.

verses.kjv: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. And he said, Neither hath the Lord chosen this.
verses.decoded: Then Jesse had Shammah pass by. And he said, The LORD has not chosen this one either.

verses.kjv: Again, Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said unto Jesse, The Lord hath not chosen these.
verses.decoded: Again, Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse, The LORD has not chosen these.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Send and fetch him: for we will not sit down till he come hither.
verses.decoded: And Samuel said to Jesse, Are all your children here? And he said, The youngest is still here, and he is taking care of the sheep. And Samuel said to Jesse, Send and bring him, because we will not sit down until he comes here.

verses.kjv: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the Lord said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.
verses.decoded: So he sent for him and brought him in. Now he had a reddish complexion, and he was handsome and good-looking. Then the LORD said, 'Get up and anoint him, because this is the one.'

verses.kjv: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
verses.decoded: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him among his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward. Then Samuel got up and went to Ramah.

verses.kjv: But the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him.
verses.decoded: But the Spirit of the LORD left Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD caused him distress.

verses.kjv: And Saul’s servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee.
verses.decoded: And Saul’s servants said to him, Look now, an evil spirit from God is troubling you.

verses.kjv: Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.
verses.decoded: Let our lord now tell your servants who are in front of you to find a man who is skilled at playing the harp, and it will happen that when the evil spirit from God is on you, he will play with his hand, and you will feel better.

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto his servants, Provide me now a man that can play well, and bring him to me.
verses.decoded: And Saul said to his servants, Find me a man who can play well, and bring him to me.

verses.kjv: Then answered one of the servants, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Beth-lehemite, that is cunning in playing, and a mighty valiant man, and a man of war, and prudent in matters, and a comely person, and the Lord is with him.
verses.decoded: Then one of the servants answered and said, Look, I have seen a son of Jesse from Bethlehem, who is skillful at playing music, a very brave man, a warrior, wise in understanding, good-looking, and the LORD is with him.

verses.kjv: Wherefore Saul sent messengers unto Jesse, and said, Send me David thy son, which is with the sheep.
verses.decoded: Therefore Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.

verses.kjv: And Jesse took an ass laden with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid, and sent them by David his son unto Saul.
verses.decoded: Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a bottle of wine, and a young goat, and sent them with David his son to Saul.

verses.kjv: And David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armourbearer.
verses.decoded: David went to Saul and stood in front of him. Saul loved David very much, and David became his armor-bearer.

verses.kjv: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David, I pray thee, stand before me; for he hath found favour in my sight.
verses.decoded: And Saul sent a message to Jesse, saying, Please let David stand before me, because he has found favor in my eyes.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
verses.decoded: When the evil spirit from God came upon Saul, David took a harp and played it with his hand. Saul felt refreshed and well, and the evil spirit left him.

verses.kjv: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle, and were gathered together at Shochoh, which belongeth to Judah, and pitched between Shochoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.
verses.decoded: Now the Philistines gathered their armies for battle and assembled at Shochoh, which belongs to Judah, and camped between Shochoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.

verses.kjv: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and pitched by the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.
verses.decoded: Saul and the men of Israel gathered together, camped in the valley of Elah, and arranged their army to fight against the Philistines.

verses.kjv: And the Philistines stood on a mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on a mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.
verses.decoded: The Philistines stood on a mountain on one side, and Israel stood on a mountain on the other side, with a valley between them.

verses.kjv: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
verses.decoded: A warrior came out from the Philistine camp named Goliath, from Gath, who was six cubits and a span tall.

verses.kjv: And he had an helmet of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
verses.decoded: He had a bronze helmet on his head, and he was wearing a coat of armor; the coat weighed five thousand shekels of bronze.

verses.kjv: And he had greaves of brass upon his legs, and a target of brass between his shoulders.
verses.decoded: He wore bronze armor on his legs, and a bronze shield was strapped between his shoulders.

verses.kjv: And the staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and one bearing a shield went before him.
verses.decoded: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s rod, and the iron point of his spear weighed six hundred shekels. A man carrying a shield walked in front of him.

verses.kjv: And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, Why are ye come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.
verses.decoded: And he stood and shouted to the armies of Israel, and said to them, Why have you come out to arrange your battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.

verses.kjv: If he be able to fight with me, and to kill me, then will we be your servants: but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall ye be our servants, and serve us.
verses.decoded: If he can fight me and kill me, then we will be your servants; but if I defeat him and kill him, then you will be our servants and serve us.

verses.kjv: And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.
verses.decoded: And the Philistine said, I challenge the armies of Israel today; send me a man so that we can fight each other.

verses.kjv: When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.
verses.decoded: When Saul and all the people of Israel heard what the Philistine said, they were upset and very afraid.

verses.kjv: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons: and the man went among men for an old man in the days of Saul.
verses.decoded: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite from Bethlehem in Judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons. The man was considered old among the people during the days of Saul.

verses.kjv: And the three eldest sons of Jesse went and followed Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons that went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and next unto him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
verses.decoded: The three oldest sons of Jesse went and followed Saul to the battle. The names of the three sons who went to the battle were Eliab, the firstborn, then Abinadab, and the third was Shammah.

verses.kjv: And David was the youngest: and the three eldest followed Saul.
verses.decoded: David was the youngest, and the three oldest brothers went with Saul.

verses.kjv: But David went and returned from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Beth-lehem.
verses.decoded: But David went away and came back from Saul to take care of his father's sheep in Bethlehem.

verses.kjv: And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.
verses.decoded: The Philistine came near every morning and evening and showed himself for forty days.

verses.kjv: And Jesse said unto David his son, Take now for thy brethren an ephah of this parched corn, and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to thy brethren;
verses.decoded: And Jesse said to David his son, Take now for your brothers an ephah of this roasted grain, and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to your brothers;

verses.kjv: And carry these ten cheeses unto the captain of their thousand, and look how thy brethren fare, and take their pledge.
verses.decoded: And take these ten cheeses to the leader of their thousand, see how your brothers are doing, and get their guarantee.

verses.kjv: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel, were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.
verses.decoded: Now Saul, they, and all the men of Israel were in the valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines.

verses.kjv: And David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took, and went, as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the trench, as the host was going forth to the fight, and shouted for the battle.
verses.decoded: David got up early in the morning, left the sheep with a shepherd, and took what Jesse had told him to take. Then he went to the battlefield, where the army was going out to fight, and shouted to join the battle.

verses.kjv: For Israel and the Philistines had put the battle in array, army against army.
verses.decoded: Israel and the Philistines had arranged their armies for battle, army against army.

verses.kjv: And David left his carriage in the hand of the keeper of the carriage, and ran into the army, and came and saluted his brethren.
verses.decoded: David left his chariot with the chariot driver, ran into the army, and came to greet his brothers.

verses.kjv: And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the armies of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.
verses.decoded: While he was talking with them, the champion, the Philistine from Gath named Goliath, came up from the Philistine army and spoke the same words. David heard him.

verses.kjv: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.
verses.decoded: All the men of Israel, when they saw the man, ran away from him and were very afraid.

verses.kjv: And the men of Israel said, Have ye seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, that the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.
verses.decoded: And the men of Israel said, Have you seen this man who has come up? Surely he has come up to challenge Israel. And it will happen that the man who kills him, the king will reward him with great wealth, and will give him his daughter, and will exempt his father's house from taxes in Israel.

verses.kjv: And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?
verses.decoded: And David spoke to the men standing near him, saying, What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes the disgrace from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine that he should challenge the armies of the living God?

verses.kjv: And the people answered him after this manner, saying, So shall it be done to the man that killeth him.
verses.decoded: And the people answered him in this way, saying, This is what will be done to the man who kills him.

verses.kjv: And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spake unto the men; and Eliab’s anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle.
verses.decoded: And Eliab, his oldest brother, heard him talking to the men; and Eliab became angry with David and said, Why did you come down here? And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and the wickedness of your heart, because you have come down to see the battle.

verses.kjv: And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause?
verses.decoded: And David said, What have I done now? Is there not a reason?

verses.kjv: And he turned from him toward another, and spake after the same manner: and the people answered him again after the former manner.
verses.decoded: He turned from him to someone else and spoke in the same way, and the people answered him again in the same manner as before.

verses.kjv: And when the words were heard which David spake, they rehearsed them before Saul: and he sent for him.
verses.decoded: When the words that David spoke were heard, they repeated them to Saul, and Saul sent for him.

verses.kjv: And David said to Saul, Let no man’s heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.
verses.decoded: And David said to Saul, Do not let anyone be afraid because of him; I will go and fight this Philistine.

verses.kjv: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.
verses.decoded: And Saul said to David, You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight him because you are only a young man, and he is a warrior from his youth.

verses.kjv: And David said unto Saul, Thy servant kept his father’s sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock:
verses.decoded: And David said to Saul, Your servant took care of his father’s sheep, and a lion came, and a bear came, and took a lamb from the flock:

verses.kjv: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him.
verses.decoded: And I went out after him, and struck him, and took the prey from his mouth; and when he got up against me, I grabbed him by his beard, and struck him, and killed him.

verses.kjv: Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.
verses.decoded: Your servant killed both the lion and the bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he has insulted the armies of the living God.

verses.kjv: David said moreover, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the Lord be with thee.
verses.decoded: David said further, The LORD who rescued me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said to David, Go, and may the LORD be with you.

verses.kjv: And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.
verses.decoded: Saul put his armor on David, placing a bronze helmet on his head and also equipping him with a coat of mail.

verses.kjv: And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him.
verses.decoded: And David strapped his sword onto his armor, and he tried to walk with it; because he had not tested it. And David said to Saul, I cannot go with these; because I have not tested them. And David took them off.

verses.kjv: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd’s bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.
verses.decoded: He took his staff in his hand, selected five smooth stones from the stream, put them into the shepherd’s bag he had, which was a small pouch; his sling was in his hand, and he approached the Philistine.

verses.kjv: And the Philistine came on and drew near unto David; and the man that bare the shield went before him.
verses.decoded: The Philistine advanced and approached David; the man carrying the shield walked in front of him.

verses.kjv: And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and of a fair countenance.
verses.decoded: When the Philistine looked around and saw David, he looked down on him because he was only a young man, with a reddish complexion and a handsome appearance.

verses.kjv: And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.decoded: And the Philistine said to David, Am I a dog that you come to me with sticks? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

verses.kjv: And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.
verses.decoded: And the Philistine said to David, Come here to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and to the animals of the field.

verses.kjv: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
verses.decoded: Then David said to the Philistine, You come to me with a sword, a spear, and a shield, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.

verses.kjv: This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee; and I will give the carcases of the host of the Philistines this day unto the fowls of the air, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.
verses.decoded: Today the LORD will hand you over to me; I will strike you down and cut off your head. I will give the bodies of the Philistine army today to the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth, so that everyone on earth will know that there is a God in Israel.

verses.kjv: And all this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s, and he will give you into our hands.
verses.decoded: And everyone here will know that the LORD does not save by sword and spear, because the battle belongs to the LORD, and he will hand you over to us.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose, and came and drew nigh to meet David, that David hasted, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
verses.decoded: When the Philistine stood up and came closer to meet David, David quickly ran toward the army to face the Philistine.

verses.kjv: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
verses.decoded: And David put his hand into his bag, took out a stone, and threw it, hitting the Philistine in the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell face down to the ground.

verses.kjv: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.
verses.decoded: So David defeated the Philistine with a sling and a stone, and struck the Philistine down and killed him; but David did not have a sword in his hand.

verses.kjv: Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath thereof, and slew him, and cut off his head therewith. And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.
verses.decoded: So David ran and stood over the Philistine, took his sword, pulled it out of its sheath, killed him, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they ran away.

verses.kjv: And the men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines, until thou come to the valley, and to the gates of Ekron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron.
verses.decoded: The men of Israel and Judah stood up, shouted, and chased the Philistines all the way to the valley and to the gates of Ekron. The wounded Philistines fell along the road to Shaaraim, as far as Gath and Ekron.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they spoiled their tents.
verses.decoded: The people of Israel came back after pursuing the Philistines, and they took goods from their tents.

verses.kjv: And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem; but he put his armour in his tent.
verses.decoded: And David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, but he put the armor in his tent.

verses.kjv: And when Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he said unto Abner, the captain of the host, Abner, whose son is this youth? And Abner said, As thy soul liveth, O king, I cannot tell.
verses.decoded: When Saul saw David go out to fight the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army, "Abner, whose son is this young man?" And Abner said, "As surely as you live, O king, I do not know."

verses.kjv: And the king said, Inquire thou whose son the stripling is.
verses.decoded: And the king said, Find out whose son the young man is.

verses.kjv: And as David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, Abner took him, and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
verses.decoded: When David came back from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him to Saul, holding the Philistine's head in his hand.

verses.kjv: And Saul said to him, Whose son art thou, thou young man? And David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Beth-lehemite.
verses.decoded: And Saul said to him, Whose son are you, young man? And David answered, I am the son of your servant Jesse from Bethlehem.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
verses.decoded: After he finished speaking to Saul, Jonathan's soul became closely connected to David's soul, and Jonathan loved him as much as he loved himself.

verses.kjv: And Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father’s house.
verses.decoded: And Saul took him that day, and would not allow him to return to his father's house anymore.

verses.kjv: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
verses.decoded: Then Jonathan and David made a promise to each other because Jonathan loved David as much as he loved his own life.

verses.kjv: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.
verses.decoded: Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his clothes, his sword, his bow, and his belt.

verses.kjv: And David went out whithersoever Saul sent him, and behaved himself wisely: and Saul set him over the men of war, and he was accepted in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul’s servants.
verses.decoded: And David went wherever Saul sent him, and acted wisely; and Saul put him in charge of the soldiers, and he was well regarded by all the people and also by Saul’s servants.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass as they came, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, that the women came out of all cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tabrets, with joy, and with instruments of musick.
